short_description: Not an organism: a 1931 g lump of Martian orthopyroxenite found in the Allan Hills, Antarctica, on 27 December 1984. In 1996 a NASA team led by David McKay reported four findings in it that together looked like traces of past life. Every one of the four now has a non-biological explanation. The subject is in the atlas because the testing is the lesson.

rock_facts.mass_note: 1931 g per the NASA Martian Meteorite Compendium (Meyer 2012); '1.93 kg' is the same figure rounded.
rock_facts.found: 27 December 1984, Far Western Icefield, Allan Hills, Antarctica, on a snowmobile traverse by the ANSMET field party; catalogued as field sample 1539.
rock_facts.classification: Orthopyroxenite (cumulate). ~97 vol% orthopyroxene (Fs27.3 Wo3.3 En69.4) in grains up to 6 mm, ~2% euhedral chromite, ~1% augite, olivine, pyrite, apatite, plagioclase (largely shocked to maskelynite/glass), phosphate and silica. Weathering category A/B, fracturing category B.
rock_facts.appearance_exterior: ANSMET field note: 'highly-shocked, grayish-green achondrite, 90% covered with fusion crust'. On the NASA specimen photographs the crust reads dark grey-brown rather than glossy black, and is spalled over the hackly end, exposing the interior.
rock_facts.appearance_interior: Uniform, coarse-grained, GREENISH-GREY, blocky texture (Score & MacPherson 1985). Black euhedral chromite specks; small patches of brown/orange Fe-rich carbonate.
rock_facts.crystallisation_age: 4.091 +/- 0.030 Ga (Lu-Hf internal mineral isochron, Lapen et al. 2010). Earlier Sm-Nd work suggested ~4.5 Ga; the modern consensus is ~4.09 Ga.
rock_facts.ejection_age: Cosmic-ray exposure age 15.0 +/- 0.8 Ma (Nyquist et al. 2001, averaging Eugster 15, Miura 14.5, Murty 16.4, Swindle 15.8, Garrison & Bogard 14.1, Bogard 16-18, Terribilini 15.8/15.5 Ma). See corrections: the popular '~17 Ma' sits at the top of the spread, not at the consensus.
rock_facts.terrestrial_age: ~13,000 years (Jull et al. 1995, recalculated 14C after leaching to separate carbon components; earlier 14C results gave ~6.5 ka).
rock_facts.martian_origin_basis: Oxygen-isotope analysis (Clayton 1993, Antarctic Meteorite Newsletter 16(4)), supported by Fe3+-bearing chromite, pyrite rather than troilite, and an Fe/Mn ratio wrong for a diogenite (Berkley & Boynton 1992; Mittlefehldt 1993, 1994). It was originally MISclassified as a diogenite in 1985. See corrections: the Viking-atmosphere gas match is the argument that ties the SNC clan to Mars (EETA 79001 impact glass, Bogard & Johnson 1983), NOT how ALH 84001 itself was assigned.

carbonate_rosettes.size: 100-250 micrometres across; ~0.5% of the rock by volume.
carbonate_rosettes.habit: Concentric spheroids inside the igneous rock and 'pancake-like' disks along natural fractures (Romanek et al. 1995; D. McKay et al. 1996; Scott et al. 1998).
carbonate_rosettes.zoning_optical: Dark orange core -> light orange -> BLACK -> WHITE -> BLACK, the 'Oreo cookie' rim (Meyer 2012 compendium).
carbonate_rosettes.zoning_chemical: Ca- and Fe-rich (with Mn) core grading to Mg-rich; the black outer zones (~1-5 um) are Fe- and S-rich and carry fine single-domain MAGNETITE plus sulfide (pyrrhotite, tentatively greigite, grains ~100 nm); the white sandwich zone is nearly pure magnesite with crystal faces projecting outward.
carbonate_rosettes.why_it_matters: The 1996 claim is located in these outermost black rims, not in the rock at large.

the_1996_claim.paper: McKay D.S., Gibson E.K. Jr., Thomas-Keprta K.L., Vali H., Romanek C.S., Clemett S.J., Chillier X.D.F., Maechling C.R., Zare R.N. (1996) 'Search for Past Life on Mars: Possible Relic Biogenic Activity in Martian Meteorite ALH84001.' Science 273, 924-930.
the_1996_claim.title_is_hedged: The paper's own title says 'Possible Relic'. It was presented as a hypothesis, not a finding.
four_observations: Carbonate globules/rosettes formed by low-temperature aqueous alteration on Mars.
Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) concentrated in and around the carbonate.
Magnetite and iron-sulfide crystals in the black rims, in shapes resembling those made by magnetotactic bacteria.
Segmented, elongated and ovoid shapes 20-100 nm across on fracture surfaces, interpreted as 'nanofossils'.

counter_explanations.counter: Size: at 20-100 nm they are below the floor a free-living, DNA-based cell needs to hold ribosomes and a genome. NRC 1999 workshop consensus 200-300 nm; Panel 1's formal statement 250 +/- 50 nm; 200 nm only as an extreme lower bound under relaxed assumptions.
counter_explanations.source: National Research Council (1999), 'Size Limits of Very Small Microorganisms: Proceedings of a Workshop', doi:10.17226/9638.

counter_explanations.counter: Origin: most of the elongated segmented forms are non-biological LAMELLAR GROWTH STEPS / cleavage lamellae on pyroxene and carbonate crystals; the beaded segmentation is attributed to the conductive heavy-metal (Au/Pd) coating decorating a linear crystallographic step. McKay et al.'s reply conceded that numerous crystallographic features do exist on these surfaces. Note the coating point is contested: a later controlled experiment imaged the same areas before and after Au/Pd coating and concluded the structures were not purely a coating artefact.
counter_explanations.source: Bradley J.P., Harvey R.P., McSween H.Y. Jr. (1997) 'No nanofossils in martian meteorite', Nature 390, 454-455, doi:10.1038/37257; reply McKay, Gibson, Thomas-Keprta & Vali (1997) Nature 390, 455-456.

counter_explanations.counter: PAHs form abiotically, are common in carbonaceous meteorites and in the interstellar medium, and Antarctic meltwater contamination cannot be excluded for a stone that lay in ice for ~13,000 years.
counter_explanations.source: General meteoritics; see also Steele et al. 2022 below.

counter_explanations.counter: 3D morphologies of ~1000 magnetite crystals from (a) laboratory thermal decomposition of hydrothermally precipitated Fe-rich carbonate, (b) ALH 84001 carbonate globules and (c) magnetotactic strain MV-1 showed the ALH 84001 crystals are reproduced by the INORGANIC route and differ from the commonest biogenic morphology. Reaction 3FeCO3 -> Fe3O4 + CO + 2CO2.
counter_explanations.source: Golden D.C., Ming D.W., Lauer H.V., Morris R.V., Treiman A.H., Gibson E.K. (2004) American Mineralogist 89, 681-695, doi:10.2138/am-2004-5-602.

counter_explanations.counter: Co-located nanoscale imaging, isotopic analysis and spectroscopy showed complex refractory organic material sitting in mineral assemblages produced by SERPENTINISATION and CARBONATION - water-rock reactions - and co-located with nanophase magnetite. Abiotic organic synthesis was operating on Mars ~4 Ga ago.
counter_explanations.source: Steele A. et al. (2022) 'Organic synthesis associated with serpentinization and carbonation on early Mars', Science 375, 172-177, doi:10.1126/science.abg7905.

scope_statement: What is refuted is the claim about THIS ROCK. Whether Mars ever hosted life is not settled by this and remains open; it is exactly the question Curiosity and Perseverance are on the surface to investigate. Never write or imply 'there was no life on Mars'.
tone_rule: No debunking sneer, no 'scientists were fooled', no hoax framing. The 1996 measurements were real; the interpretation over-reached and the paper said 'Possible' in its own title. The scrutiny sharpened the definition of a biosignature and helped launch modern astrobiology (NASA Astrobiology Institute founded 1998).

colour_legend._rule: One mapping used across all four styles so the set reads as one poster.
colour_legend.orthopyroxene_matrix: greenish-grey, olive-grey (#6E7368 to #8A8F80), coarse blocky grains with cleavage glints
colour_legend.carbonate_core: dark orange (#C4702F) grading to light orange (#E0A461)
colour_legend.magnetite: tiny charcoal specks confined to the black band
colour_legend.sem_false_colour: cool blue-grey substrate, warm ochre/tan on raised knobs — mineral, not tissue

do_not_draw: any living or cell-like body: no plump turgid rounded cell, no membrane, no cytoplasm, no organelles, no nucleus, no cell wall
flagella, cilia, pili, tentacles or any appendage
a swimming, crawling or otherwise motile posture; anything with a head end
eyes, a face, a mouth, or any anthropomorphic feature (except deliberately in the coloring page, which is a separate register)
glow, bioluminescence, halo, aura or backlit translucency on the segmented shapes
colonies, biofilms, mats or chains of cell-like bodies
planets, a Mars globe, starfields, nebulae, spacecraft, rovers, landers, astronauts, alien figures, flying saucers
green slime or 'alien green' colour cues
fossil-bone, amber-inclusion or dinosaur-fossil visual language
lettering, numerals, scale bars, arrows, cross-hairs, NASA-style caption strips, agency logos, watermarks
border, frame, vignette, letterbox bar, mat, drop shadow, or the artwork drawn as a sheet lying on a surface
a glossy jet-black obsidian-like fusion crust (the real crust is dark grey-brown, matte and hackly, and is spalled at one end)
an interior that is brown or red like Martian soil (the interior is greenish-grey)

reference.chosen: NASA/JSC frame 96-12609, the 'Mars worm' SEM image
reference.modality: SEM (scanning electron micrograph, greyscale, of a fracture surface in ALH 84001)
reference.attribution: NASA / Johnson Space Center; credited by APOD as D. McKay (NASA/JSC), K. Thomas-Keprta (Lockheed-Martin), R. Zare (Stanford), NASA
reference.provenance_caveat: This specific frame was released by NASA on 9 August 1996 and was NOT one of the figures in the 16 August 1996 Science paper — NASA's own caption says so: 'Although this structure is not part of the research published in the Aug. 16 issue of the journal Science, it is located in a similar carbonate glob in the meteorite.' It is the image that made the story public, not a figure from the paper.
reference.what_it_shows: A knobbly, granular mineral surface with one elongated segmented ridge running diagonally across it, plus several bright angular mineral fragments. The segmented ridge is the DISPUTED shape, not a confirmed fossil.
